items.title: DDR4 or DDR5 in 2026? Gigabyte Executive Advice As The AI Memory Shortage Drags On
points: That’s what stood out most when the Gigabyte team took the stage for their 40th anniversary.
Sunil Grewal, who heads Gigabyte India, told the gathering that memory used to be about 15% of a PC’s total cost.
Now, in some builds, it’s jumped to 40 or even 45%.
In early 2025, a 32GB DDR5 kit could be found for around ₹6,500.
By July 2026, popular 32GB DDR5-6000 kits were selling for about ₹40,000 on Amazon India.
Even 32GB DDR4-3200 kits, the older and supposedly “stable” option, were selling for roughly ₹25,000 to ₹27,000.
Gartner estimates that memory will peak at 23% of a PC’s bill of materials in 2026, up from 16% in 2025.
Gartner expects combined DRAM and SSD prices to rise about 130% by the end of 2026, and average PC prices to rise 17% compared with 2025.

items.title: G7 launches 14-port alliance to tackle global drug trafficking
points: Fourteen major ports are joining forces in a new G7-backed initiative aimed at combating drug trafficking through international shipping networks, with artificial intelligence and closer intelligence sharing central to the programme.
The G7+ Ports Network was formally launched yesterday in Marseille, bringing together the world’s leading industrialised economies alongside Brazil and South Korea.

The initiative connects port authorities, customs organisations and law enforcement agencies in an attempt to identify suspicious container movements and disrupt the maritime routes used by organised crime.
Participants include ports in Marseille, Le Havre, Dunkirk, Hamburg, Genoa, Busan and Houston.
International organisations involved include Interpol, the International Maritime Organization, the World Customs Organization and the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime.
The initiative was first proposed at June’s G7 summit in Évian, where leaders identified maritime transport as a principal route for international trafficking in narcotics and precursor chemicals.
According to Barrot, approximately 70% of illegal drugs entering France arrive through ports, highlighting the challenge of screening enormous container volumes without disrupting legitimate trade.

items.title: Nintendo Steps Up Game Preservation Efforts Before Its History Is Lost
points: Nintendo is taking steps to preserve decades of its gaming legacy.
The role involves interviewing longtime employees to ensure their valuable knowledge about the company’s older projects is not lost over time.
The move further highlights Nintendo’s commitment to its gaming legacy, especially since it has no plans to abandon physical games.
On the official Nintendo career page, the company has shared a job listing for a “Digital Archivist, Historical Systems” to preserve information about its older gaming platforms.
The listing went live in November 2026 and is an approximately 12-month contract-based job in Redmond, Washington.
This will contain historical technical records, engineering documents, and software development materials for games like Super Mario, Zelda, Pikmin, and more.
Such materials could potentially be useful for remasters, remakes, or other projects involving classic games, similar to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.

items.title: Kerala HC allows hotel Radisson Blu in Kochi to operate till 3 a.m.

items.title: The dirty secret of shipping’s clean hull ambitions
points: Hull fouling drives up fuel bills and emissions, yet ports increasingly restrict the very cleaning operations needed to tackle it.
The missing piece is a global network of places where ships can safely get cleaned.
Once cleaning is restricted, the ship may keep sailing with the dirty hull.
In the scenario studied, a slime layer as thin as 0.5 millimetres covering up to half a hull can raise greenhouse-gas emissions by about 25 to 30%, depending on ship type, speed and conditions.
Owners diverted to Bundaberg, Australia, for hull cleaning.
A vessel had already undergone underwater inspection and cleaning in West Africa before a New Zealand call.

Under BIMCO’s 2019 Hull Fouling Clause for time charters, where the clause applies and cleaning is called for following an inspection, speed and consumption warranties can remain suspended if cleaning at the place of inspection is not permitted or possible.
DNV, in April 2025, put light slime at up to 20% extra fuel consumption and heavy shell fouling at up to 85%.

items.title: India launches probe into dumping of aluminium products from China, Malaysia, Vietnam

"In view of the foregoing, and having satisfied itself, on the basis of the information furnished by ALEMAI and its member producers, the Authority hereby suo motu initiates an anti-dumping investigation," the DGTR notification dated November 9 said.

In the probe, the directorate will determine the existence, degree and effect of the alleged dumping of the product and recommend the amount of anti-dumping duty that, if levied, would adequately remove the injury to the domestic industry.

points: File photo shows children celebrating Deepavali by bursting crackers in Nellore.

This year Cyclone Murasu played spoilsport on Deepavali celebrations across Nellore., Prakasam and Markapuram districts. | Photo Credit: The Hindu Cyclone Murasu has played spoilsport on Deepavali celebrations across SPSR Nellore, Prakasam and Markapuram…
Heavy downpour and power cuts have dampened the festival spirit among everyone, right from kids to elderly people and farmers to retail vendors.
Generally, households purchase crackers and diyas (earthenware lamps) on Deepavali morning or a day ahead.
The power cuts led to mosquito menace at homes.
Despite of the swift restoration works in progress, the power supply was not yet rectified in the rural areas by Monday (November 9, 2026) evening.
They revealed that they were using kerosene lamps during night times.
The devastating wind and rains have flattened chilli and paddy crops to the ground in Purumetla village of Mundlamuru mandal, and Chinna Kothapalli village of Addanki mandal.

items.title: All TVK MLAs summoned to Chennai as CM Vijay chairs key meeting to discuss attack on deputy speaker
points: All Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) MLAs have been summoned to Chennai in connection with the Deputy Speaker attack issue and the prevailing situation in Kallakurichi district.
A consultative meeting is expected to be held on November 11 at the party headquarters in Panaiyur, led by Chief Minister Joseph Vijay and Minister N.
The meeting is expected to discuss the two issues in detail, with the party leadership likely to issue strict instructions to all MLAs on handling the situation and maintaining discipline.

This development came after a man who was allegedly assaulted by Tamil Nadu Deputy Speaker Ravi Shankar was admitted to Mahatma Gandhi Memorial Government Hospital in Tiruchirappalli for further treatment.

Karthik Kumar, a resident of Kannabiran Colony in Thuraiyur, Tiruchirappalli district, said he had repeatedly approached the municipal administration regarding the lack of basic amenities in his locality, but no action had been taken.
On noticing the car of Deputy Speaker Ravi Shankar parked there, he approached him to raise complaints about the problems in his locality.

items.title: Asian Stock Markets Today 10 Nov Tuesday: Kospi up 5%, Nikkei jumps 4% after Wall Street's best day in 7 months; factors
points: Asian stocks today: Asian equity markets traded sharply higher on Tuesday, tracking a strong overnight rally on Wall Street, where technology shares staged a recovery and falling crude oil prices helped US benchmarks record their best session in seven months.
MSCI Inc. ’s gauge of regional equities climbed 1.6%.
South Korea's Kospi Index jumped more than 5% in early trading, while Japan's Nikkei 225 advanced nearly 4%.

The recovery in Japan followed a nearly 6% decline in the Nikkei on Friday, when artificial intelligence-related stocks came under intense selling pressure.
Technology investor SoftBank Group surged 14.38% on Tuesday, while semiconductor equipment makers Advantest and Tokyo Electron gained 4.93% and 5.66%, respectively.

items.title: Take-Two CEO Addresses GTA 6 Disc Release, Says Decision Is up to Rockstar
points: There’s been quite a bit of commotion around GTA 6’s release, particularly because its physical version doesn’t come with a disc but instead comes with a digital download code.
In other words, the biggest entertainment release of the decade won’t have a physical disc at launch, though Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick has addressed the debacle.

The CEO also told Variety that GTA 6’s presales have exceeded expectations, but didn’t provide an update on whether GTA 6 will eventually get a traditional disc edition or when it would come to PC or the Switch 2.
Still, that hasn’t stopped players from buying the game, whether it’s the GTA 6 Standard Edition or the GTA 6 Ultimate Edition.
Despite GTA 6’s digital-only release, Take-Two reported $1.38 billion in game revenue for the July–September quarter, according to Variety.
As for a possible GTA 6 disc release, PC launch, or Nintendo Switch 2 release, Rockstar will share any updates in the future.

items.title: Nine Shigella cases confirmed in Malappuram; Health dept. steps up preventive measures
points: The Health department has stepped up preventive measures in Malappuram district following an outbreak of Shigella infection, with nine cases confirmed so far.
Cleaning operations, including super-chlorination of wells and houses in the affected areas, are under way.
The family health centre at Elamkulam, near Perinthalmanna, formed a special squad to conduct house-to-house surveillance and create awareness about the infection.
The outbreak came to light after more than 100 people who attended a wedding at Elamkulam on October 31 reported symptoms.
In a separate development, a four-year-old girl from Fifth Mile in Amarambalam panchayat, Nilambur, tested positive for Shigella.
Following this, the Health department imposed restrictions on evening tea shops and street food stalls in the area.

Apart from those who attended the wedding, the confirmed cases include the four-year-old girl who ate snacks from a shop at Amarambalam and two people who had mandi from a restaurant at Palunda, Nilambur.

items.title: Keralam cardiologists seek review of order banning re-use of single-use medical devices
points: Prathap Kumar N., organising chairman of the conference, said the rising cost of complex angioplasty, particularly procedures requiring multiple specialised devices, had become a major concern.
Reimbursement package rates under government-funded health insurance schemes were often inadequate to cover the actual cost of advanced cardiac interventions.
With an increasing proportion of the population requiring advanced cardiac interventions, making complex procedures affordable to ordinary patients was a major challenge.
Any proposal for re-use must be supported by scientific evidence, validated sterilisation, functional testing and strict regulatory oversight,” Dr. Prathap Kumar said.

He called for wider consultation among medical specialists, infection-control experts and regulatory authorities to develop an evidence-based policy regarding the sterilisation and re-use of medical devices, balancing affordability with patient safety.

The order by the DGHS said the practice of re-using single-use devices and disposable surgical items was a serious concern from the perspective of patient safety, infection prevention and control, regulatory compliance and healthcare expenditure.

items.title: Three killed, one injured as ‘speeding’ SUV hits motorcycle in UP’s Kannauj: Police
points: Three men were killed and another injured after the motorcycle they were travelling on was hit by an allegedly speeding SUV in Uttar Pradesh’s Kannauj late on Monday, police said on Tuesday.
Eyewitnesses said the impact was so severe that all four men were thrown 15-20 metres away, and the motorcycle was completely mangled.
None of the deceased were wearing a helmet.
The SUV, which was allegedly coming from the wrong side of the road, fled the spot immediately after the crash and efforts are underway to trace the vehicle, the police said.
In a post on X, Kannauj police said the accident took place in Indergarh police station area, around 35 km from the district headquarters.
The four men were rushed to the medical college in Tirwa, where doctors declared three of them dead.
Local residents and eyewitnesses said the four friends left their houses at around 11.20pm on Monday and were crossing Sardar Patel Inter College when the SUV arrived from the wrong side.

items.title: NMC cautions students against fake medical colleges, asks them to verify approvals
points: In a recent advisory issued in compliance with directions from the Supreme Court, the NMC has urged students to independently verify a medical college’s approval status, permitted student intake, and admission permissions for the relevant academic year…
The advisory follows the Supreme Court taking cognisance of the issue in Ayesha Jain v.

Amity University, Noida & Ors., an ongoing case in which the Court directed regulatory bodies, including the NMC, to caution students and parents against dealing with unauthorised educational institutions.
The directions came in the context of a reported instance of a purported fake medical college operating from a farmhouse and claiming to offer various courses.

The Commission has clarified that a medical college’s presence in an official list, or its previous operation, does not automatically establish that it has permission to admit students in subsequent academic years.
Candidates must check the approval granted for the particular year and the number of seats sanctioned through official NMC and Medical Assessment and Rating Board (MARB) records.

items.title: Meta’s Muse Personal AI Agent Pricing for India Revealed Ahead of Debut: Report
points: Meta has revealed the India pricing of the Muse personal AI agent, according to a report.
On the other hand, the higher-end Maximum plan is said to cost Rs 8,999.
However, the report does not specify whether these prices are for monthly or yearly payment plans.
In the US, the company only offers monthly payment options for both tiers at similar prices: $20 (roughly Rs 1,900) and $100 (about Rs 9,400), respectively.
According to Meta’s website, globally, the Power tier offers 500 million Muse tokens per week.
On the other hand, the Max plan provides 3 billion Muse tokens every week.

items.title: Upcoming IPOs: SEBI clears 8 issues, including Mahanadi Coalfields, Veritas Finance and Sagar Defence; details here
points: The list includes state-owned Mahanadi Coalfields, non-banking financial company Veritas Finance, defence technology player Sagar Defence Engineering, fintech major Razorpay and MakeMyTrip's India subsidiary.
Veritas Finance Ltd, a non-deposit-taking non-banking financial company (NBFC), has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to launch its IPO.
The company had initially filed draft papers with SEBI in January 2025, proposing to raise ₹2,800 crore through an IPO.
State-owned Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd (MCL), an Odisha-based subsidiary of Coal India, has secured SEBI's clearance for its proposed IPO.

The public issue will be entirely an offer for sale of up to 66,18,36,300 equity shares by its promoter, Coal India Ltd. Since the IPO is an OFS, Mahanadi Coalfields will not receive any proceeds from the issue.
Pharmaceutical company Encube Ethicals is planning to raise around ₹3,000 crore through its proposed IPO.
Sagar Defence Engineering has received observations from SEBI on 4 November after filing its draft IPO papers through the confidential pre-filing route.

items.title: India's water management initiatives a model for developing nations: World Bank official
points: United Nations, India's water management initiatives have emerged as a model for developing countries, a senior World Bank official said, while lauding the country's efforts to improve access to drinking water, restore rivers, and strengthen dam safety.

Global Director for Water at the World Bank Group Saroj Kumar Jha described India's progress as a "remarkable success story", saying developing nations were looking at its experience for solutions to their water challenges.
"For the World Bank Group, India is a remarkable success story.

It's the water journey that every single developing country is looking at," Jha said in response to a PTI question during a virtual press briefing on Friday ahead of the 2026 United Nations Water Conference.

The conference, co-hosted by the United Arab Emirates and Senegal, will be held in Abu Dhabi from December 8 to 10, bringing together world leaders, policymakers and other stakeholders to strengthen international cooperation on water security and sanitation.

items.title: Anthropic plans IPO live stream with Amodei, JPMorgan CEO Dimon
points: Anthropic PBC is preparing for a live-streamed event featuring CEO Dario Amodei and JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon.
This event is aimed at marketing their upcoming initial public offering, which might break records.
The IPO is set to begin marketing shortly and is planned to debut before the Thanksgiving holiday.
Anthropic is targeting an offering size similar to SpaceX's IPO, which raised significant funding.

items.title: NSE deploys liquid cooling technology for AI infrastructure, targets 224-GPU capacity
points: NSE has already deployed multiple GPUs and plans to expand the capacity to more than 80 GPUs during the current quarter.
The infrastructure has been designed to accommodate up to 224 GPUs across high-density racks, providing scope for further expansion as the exchange scales its AI applications.

The deployment is aimed at supporting high-density GPU-based computing through a scalable cooling architecture, as AI applications place increasing demands on computing capacity, power and cooling systems.
The exchange said the on-premises infrastructure would also strengthen data sovereignty by allowing it to retain complete control over AI data, computing resources and access.

Markets closed today for Diwali-Balipratipada, trading to resume on November 11 Viral Mody, Executive Director, NSE, said the exchange was investing in advanced technologies to strengthen operational excellence, enhance efficiency and promote responsible…
Sampath Manickam, Chief Technology Officer, NSE, said AI was driving a fundamental shift in technology infrastructure, with significantly higher requirements for computing density, power and cooling.

items.title: EVs Not Very Profitable, Say Automobile Dealers
points: The Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA) says EV sales margins are low, even as showrooms invest in chargers, specialised equipment and trained staff.
He called for automobile manufacturers and dealerships to work together on a more sustainable business model.
FADA's October 2026 retail data show approximately 3.55 lakh electric vehicles sold across two-wheelers, three-wheelers, passenger cars and commercial vehicles.
That was 44.88% more than October last year.
EVs accounted for about 11.5% of all vehicle retail sales, compared with roughly 6% a year earlier.
They do not mean 11.5% of passenger cars sold were electric.
EVs accounted for around 7.3% of passenger-vehicle retail sales in October, while the electric share of three-wheelers was close to 63%.
FADA says expansion into Tier 3 and Tier 4 markets is adding to the financial pressure, although it is necessary if customers are to receive dependable service away from big cities.

items.title: Five, including four minor girls, die after drowning in lake in Tamil Nadu's Tiruvannamalai
points: A woman and four minor girls, including three sisters, drowned in a lake in Tamil Nadu's temple town of Tiruvannamalai late on Monday evening.

Police said the victims include three sisters, aged between 13 and 16; the caretaker of the government-run Children Home for Girls, identified as 29-year-old Thenmozhi; and another girl from the school, aged 16.
According to police, the three sisters, living in the Children Home for Girls, had gone to their home in nearby Karapattu village to celebrate the Deepavali festival.
The victims returned to Tiruvannamalai on Monday afternoon.

As Monday was declared a holiday by the district administration, the victims, along with the caretaker, went to the lake located near the Children Home for Girls, where they allegedly drowned in the lake without being aware of how deep it was, police said.
Police officials said that due to heavy rain in the district over the last few days, the water level in the lake has increased.

items.title: US ETFs to Buy for Samvat 2083: Samco recommends 2 ETFs with potential upside of up to 60% for Indian investors
points: In its Samvat 2083 investment strategy, Samco Wealth has recommended two US-listed exchange-traded funds (ETFs) as long-term portfolio hedges: the Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLE) and the Health Care Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLV).
Samco has assigned potential upside of 47% to XLE and 60% to XLV, with a suggested holding period of at least two years.

Benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty closed in positive territory on Monday, the first day of Samvat 2083, supported by easing crude oil prices and buying interest in heavyweight banking and financial stocks.
The 30-share BSE Sensex advanced 107.25 points, or 0.13%, to finish at 81,106.65.
Samvat 2082 was a difficult year for Indian equities, with the Nifty falling 10.9% from 25,868.60 on Muhurat Trading in 2025 to 23,053.10 on October 30, 2026.
The Sensex declined 11.8% over the same period.
The S&P 500 gained 12.5% in dollar terms and 21.9% in rupee terms, while Brent crude surged 91.8% and the rupee depreciated 8.3%.

items.title: Ex-BJD Rajya Sabha MP surrenders in abduction, murder case after top court cancels bail
points: Former Biju Janata Dal (BJD) Rajya Sabha MP N.

Bhaskar Rao on Monday surrendered before a court in Odisha’s Rayagada district, two weeks after the Supreme Court cancelled his bail in a case pertaining to the abduction and murder of a tribal leader in 2010, officials said.
Rao appeared before the Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate (SDJM) court along with three other accused — Epili Sanyasi Raju, P.
The Supreme Court on October 26 had set aside the bail granted to Bhaskar Rao by the Orissa High Court on January 22 this year and directed him to surrender before the SDJM court within two weeks.
The murder had triggered protests by the Adivasi Mahasangha in Rayagada in 2021 and 2023, with the organisation demanding a speedy and impartial investigation.
The case has been registered under sections 302 (murder), 201 (causing disappearance of evidence) and 34 (common intention) of the erstwhile Indian Penal Code.

items.title: POSH Act needs effective implementation, greater awareness in private sector: NCW chief
points: New Delhi, National Commission for Women Chairperson Vijaya Rahatkar has stressed the need for effective implementation of the POSH Act, calling for greater awareness in the private sector and ensuring that workplace committees function effectively to…
In an interview with PTI, Rahatkar described the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act as a comprehensive law but said its implementation on the ground needed to be strengthened.
"The POSH Act is a very comprehensive law.
"The Internal Committee must then examine the complaint in a time-bound manner, without any bias or prejudice, and arrive at a decision after assessing the facts," Rahatkar said.
Pointing to gaps in implementation, she said Internal Committees had been constituted in almost all government-level organisations, but greater efforts were needed to reach the private sector.
"Even today, there is not enough awareness about this law in the private sector.
"The National Commission for Women, along with all the State Women's Commissions associated with us, is working extensively on POSH.

items.title: New KTM 1390 Super Duke GT Evo Debuts – AMT, 8.8-inch TFT, Offline Sat-Nav
points: KTM has unveiled the all-new 1390 Super Duke GT Evo at EICMA 2026, which is positioned above the standard 1390 Super Duke GT.
The new model gets a range of exclusive features, while borrowing the 1,350 cc LC8 V-twin engine platform from the KTM 1390 Super Adventure S Evo.
KTM 1390 Super Duke GT Evo will go on sale across global markets in early 2027.
Engineered for sport-touring, KTM 1390 Super Duke GT Evo gets an advanced AMT transmission.
KTM 1390 Super Duke GT Evo uses a 1,350cc, 2-cylinder, V 75° engine, which is the same as in use with 1390 Super Adventure S Evo.
KTM has introduced new features with the 1390 Super Duke GT Evo to enhance rider comfort and safety.
KTM 1390 Super Duke GT Evo has 17-inch wheels at both ends, wrapped in Michelin Power 6 tires.
KTM 1390 Super Duke GT Evo gets an 8.8-inch TFT display with an easy menu structure.

items.title: VW Compact SUV For India Arriving In 2027 – What We Know So Far
points: GaadiWaadi - New Volkswagen compact SUV will share its architecture with the Skoda Kylaq and could borrow design elements from the Taigun and Virtus The Volkswagen Polo disappeared from Indian showrooms in 2022 after the Ameo compact sedan had already been…
The German manufacturer is now preparing a return to the sub-four-metre passenger vehicle category, this time in the form of an SUV.
Volkswagen confirmed the new model a few months ago and has scheduled its market introduction for 2027.
The vehicle will be developed and manufactured in India and it will sit below the Taigun as the most affordable SUV in the Volkswagen portfolio.
The exterior could take inspiration from the recently updated Taigun and the Virtus facelift which is scheduled to arrive soon.
The compact SUV could feature a similar grille treatment, prominent wheel arches, distinctive LED daytime running lamps and a redesigned rear section.
Both use the MQB A0 IN architecture developed by engineering teams in India and Europe.

items.title: MP's Hingot War tradition leaves 20 injured as participants clash during post-Diwali ritual in Indore
points: The traditional 'Hingot War' -- a fiery Diwali ritual unique to Madhya Pradesh and said to be 300-year-old -- left 20 people injured in Indore district on Monday evening, a health department official said.
Block Medical Officer (BMO) Dr Vibha Nagar told PTI that 20 'warriors' were injured during the Hingot War in Gautampura town, about 55 kilometers from Indore.
She said that six of these people were admitted to a primary health centre, while 14 people with minor burns were given first aid on the spot and sent home.
A large number of spectators gathered to witness the traditional Hingot War, held on a field in Gautampura town on the day after Diwali.
During the traditional 'Hingot War', the group of warriors from Gautampura is called "Turra," while the fighters from Runji village lead the rival "Kalangi" group.
Warriors from both groups fire burning Hingot balls at each other during the traditional battle.

items.title: HT morning brief Nov 10: Trump says Iran war 'militarily effectively over'; M John Harrison becomes oldest-ever Booker Prize winner
points: A year after the deadly blast near Delhi's Red Fort claimed 12 lives, the families of those killed are still struggling to rebuild their lives.
The November 10, 2025, explosion took place at the junction in front of Red Fort.
Investigations later found that Umar-un-Nabi, a doctor originally from Jammu and Kashmir, was allegedly inside the explosives-laden vehicle.
Nvidia and its founder, Jensen Huang, were sued on Monday by shareholders who claimed the company hid details of the CEO's alleged relationship with a businesswoman accused of being a Chinese spy.
United States President Donald Trump said on Monday that US military action in Iran is "effectively over".
The US has restricted its operation in Iran to sanctions, a naval blockade and targeted strikes since July 2026.
British author M John Harrison has won the 2026 Booker Prize for his novel ‘The End of Everything’, becoming the oldest writer to receive the prestigious literary honour at the age of 81.

items.title: India’s international air passenger traffic grows despite airspace closures, conflicts
points: India’s international air passenger traffic grew 6.1% to 78.7 million in FY-26, up from 74.7 million in 2024-25, according to data provided by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA).
Indian airlines accounted for 44.4% of international passenger traffic during the year, while foreign carriers held the remaining 55.6% share, the data showed.
IndiGo had the largest share among individual operators at 20.8%, followed by Air India at 12.9%.
Domestic passenger traffic, meanwhile, edged up to 167.4 million in the financial year ending March 2026, a modest 1.1% rise from the previous year.
Overall air passenger growth rose 2.7% at 246.1 million in the financial year 2025-26, compared with 239.7 million passengers flown by all airlines operating in the country in the previous year.
IndiGo continued to account for the largest share of domestic passenger traffic at 63%, followed by Air India at 13.6% and Air India Express at 6.3%.
International cargo traffic increased 20.6% to 21.3 lakh tonnes, compared with 17.66 lakh tonnes in the previous year.

items.title: In memoir, Sonia Gandhi recalls UPA power dynamics with Manmohan, Pranab’s 2010 PM post hint
points: Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) chairperson Sonia Gandhi has revealed in her memoir that there was always a clear division of power during the United Progressive Alliance (UPA) era, and that former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh ran the government while…

Denying that government files were ever shown to her - an allegation made in previous books - Gandhi, in ‘Belonging: A Journey of Love’ , says she gave her inputs on government formation so that those who had served the party for years when they were out…

She also reveals that she - along with her children Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra - had decided months before the 2004 general elections result that she would never become PM, something her children insisted on because of safety concerns.
Former President Pranab Mukherjee and his daughter, Sharmishtha Mukherjee, have hinted in the past about Gandhi’s reluctance to make him PM, even though he was the senior most in the UPA Cabinet.

items.title: Dyson Hot+Cool HF1 Fan, Dyson Cool Tower Fan Launched in India With Air Multiplier Technology: Price, Features
points: The Dyson Hot+Cool HF1 fan and Dyson Cool tower fan have been launched in India, the company announced on Tuesday.
The two Dyson bladeless fans will be available for purchase via the Dyson India online store and the offline Dyson Demo stores across the country, allowing customers to experience the devices.
The new Dyson Hot+Cool HF1 fan and Dyson Cool Tower fan are bladeless fans powered by the Air Multiplier technology.
Dyson’s technology is claimed to combine the principles used in turbochargers and jet engines to increase the volume of air surrounding the machines to amplify the airflow.
The Dyson Hot+Cool HF1 fan is a two-in-one model that can blow warm air during winters and cool air during summers.
The company claims that the appliance can increase the temperature of the entire room by 1 degree Celsius in about 100 seconds.

items.title: Seagems PLSV lined up for Petrobras work from 2028
points: Paratus Energy Services has confirmed that Petrobras has accepted a bid from its Seagems joint venture for the pipelay support vessel (PLSV) Jade, bringing the vessel closer to securing employment in Brazil from 2028.

The development follows the publication of the final results of Petrobras’ latest PLSV tender, which was launched earlier this year to secure offshore pipelay capacity for the Brazilian company’s subsea operations.
Paratus stressed that acceptance remains conditional on Petrobras awarding a formal contract and signing definitive agreements.
The tender comprises five packages with different technical requirements and offers potential contract periods of four years.
Seagems, in which Bermuda-based Paratus holds a 50% interest, currently operates six multipurpose pipelay support vessels under contracts in Brazil.
The company submitted bids for both Jade and an additional third-party vessel during the tender process.
In September, Petrobras accepted Seagems’ bid for the third-party unit, which the joint venture has secured access to through a memorandum of understanding that also includes a purchase option.

items.title: Fugro secures four-year extension with Heerema
points: Dutch geo-data specialist Fugro has extended its global framework agreement with Heerema Marine Contractors for another four years, continuing a partnership covering offshore installation, construction, and decommissioning projects.
The renewed deal will run from January 2027 until December 2030 and covers survey and positioning services across Heerema’s fleet of heavy-lift construction vessels.
Fugro will provide technical support for the transportation, installation and removal of offshore structures, including oil and gas platforms and offshore wind foundations.
The agreement will also use Fugro’s remote operations centres, allowing onshore specialists to monitor positioning and survey activities during offshore campaigns.
The two companies originally signed a four-year framework agreement in February 2022, covering the use of Fugro’s survey technologies on Heerema’s heavy-lift fleet.
That arrangement included QuickVision, 3Direct, and InclinoCam systems designed to improve positioning accuracy and provide remote monitoring during complex offshore operations.
At Germany’s 257MW Arcadis Ost 1 wind farm, Fugro deployed its QuickVision camera technology to help Heerema install 27 turbines using a floating rotor-nacelle assembly method.

Sonia also describes Rajiv’s reassurance during her mother-in-law’s outbursts, Indira’s domestic routines, love for sarees and photographs, and how grandchildren gradually softened her temperament.

items.title: What made Sonia Gandhi turn down PM post after UPA’s 2004 victory? Memoir revisits moment
points: Sonia Gandhi reveals her thoughts in her memoir about declining the prime minister role after the UPA's victory.
She describes her inner voice guiding her decision and her conversation with Rahul.
Gandhi highlights why she chose Manmohan Singh for the position, noting his integrity and governance experience.
Her memoir also covers her personal journey, including significant tragedies and cultural adjustments after moving to India.

items.title: India, US plan joint crackdown on transnational drug cartels, synthetic drug trade
points: Top security officials from India and the US gathered in New Delhi to address narcotics syndicates.
The discussions focused on establishing a framework to combat synthetic drug flows and secure supply chains.
NCB Director General Anurag Garg emphasized a network-centric enforcement model to target cartels and facilitators.
Both nations endorsed operational milestones, including initiatives to prevent the diversion of synthetic drug precursors.
